title: Current and Passage
premise: Ansel Iversen, a riverboat captain hiding a forged name and a stolen inheritance, runs cargo up a monsoon coast until a spring tide exposes a cave holding the wreck of the Meridian — the ship her father supposedly went down with, and the proof of who really betrayed him. Racing a salvage fleet commander who once loved her and now hunts her, she has six tides to reach the wreck before the monsoon seals it forever. In the flooded cave she finds her father's logbook, which names her mother, not a rival captain, as the saboteur — forcing Ansel to choose between the loyalty that built her identity and the truth that could destroy it. She surrenders the salvage rights to the fleet, keeps only the logbook, and finally stops running, mooring her boat in the harbor she was born to.
about_author: Isandro Sandoval is the pen name of a former tugboat deckhand turned novelist who spent a decade working the monsoon coasts of Southeast Asia before writing full-time. He lives in a converted pilot house and is known for adventure fiction steeped in tidal lore and moral undertow.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She pilots the riverboat Kestrel through a fog-bound delta, reading water no chart records, establishing her uncanny skill and her habit of never staying anywhere long. A harbor clerk asks too many questions about her registration papers. Beat: restless competence masking fear.

chapters.title: Cargo That Whispers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She accepts a suspiciously well-paid run hauling sealed crates upriver, and the client, a salvage scout named Vey, lets slip that a survey vessel is mapping the coast for wrecks. Ansel recognizes the survey ship's name from her father's era. Beat: the past tapping on the hull.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The lowest tide in a decade is forecast, and local legend says it will bare the entrance to the Hollow — a cave that 'charges admission' in drowned men's debts. Vey offers her a salvage partnership; she refuses too quickly, and he notices. Beat: the trap of curiosity.

chapters.title: The Name on the Paper
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A port inspector cross-checks her license and finds the forgery's seams. She bribes her way through with money she can't spare, realizing the salvage fleet could expose her anytime. Flashback seeds: her father's last voyage, her mother's silence. Beat: hunted in plain sight.

chapters.title: Old Charts, Older Lies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with an interlude from Vey. Ansel studies her father's surviving chart, finding annotations in two hands — his, and one she doesn't recognize. Vey, meanwhile, reports to fleet commander Rell Danforth, who requests everything on one 'Iversen.' Beat: converging lines.

chapters.title: The Harbor She Avoided
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Forced to dock at Greyhaven — her birthplace — for repairs, she walks streets where she's a ghost story. An old lockkeeper greets her by her true name, Ansel Iversen, and she doesn't correct him. Beat: the ache of being known.

chapters.title: What the Lockkeeper Kept
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The lockkeeper gives her a sealed packet her father left 'for the one who comes back by water.' Inside: a tide-table cipher pointing to the Hollow. Rell Danforth arrives in port, and Ansel watches from a distance — recognizing the man from her mother's photographs. Beat: dread with a face.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Vey dives the reef line early and finds the cave mouth's outer ledge, plus a hull timber stamped Meridian. He reports to Rell, who orders the salvage fleet mobilized — and quietly orders Ansel's boat followed. Beat: the race formally begins.

chapters.title: Running Before the Wind Shifts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She slips Greyhaven at night, using a sandbar only she knows to lose her shadow boat. But her engineer, Toma, who's been loyal for nine years, demands to know what they're actually running from. She lies; he pretends to believe her. Beat: loyalty strained by silence.

chapters.title: The First Tide
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Tide one: she reaches the outer reef and finds the fleet's buoy already planted. She dives the ledge anyway and retrieves a corroded strongbox — locked, and marked with her family crest. Beat: proof the legend is real and it's hers.

chapters.title: Toma's Ledger
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Toma opens the strongbox with a cutting torch and finds papers: her father's half of a salvage partnership signed with Rell Danforth. Toma realizes Ansel has been running from a betrayal she's never explained. Beat: the loyal man's quiet crisis.

chapters.title: Parley in the Roads
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Rell hails the Kestrel under a white flag and offers her a clean identity and a fleet commission in exchange for the cave coordinates. He calls her by her childhood nickname. She refuses — and realizes he wanted her to refuse, to justify seizing the boat. Beat: charm as a weapon.

chapters.title: Second Tide, Rising Cost
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Tide two: a storm squall forces her to choose between sheltering and diving. She dives, mapping the cave's inner passage, and finds the Meridian's mast — but the monsoon's leading edge is days early. Toma confronts her about the partnership papers. Beat: time and trust both draining.

chapters.title: The Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Studying the chart's second handwriting, Ansel finally recognizes it: her mother's. The annotations predate the wreck. She begins to suspect the sabotage story she was raised on is wrong, and that her mother knew the cave's location all along. Beat: the ground under her identity shifting.

chapters.title: Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. The salvage fleet anchors off the Hollow; Rell plans to blow the cave entrance rather than wait for tides. Vey, disturbed, feeds Ansel the schedule through an old debt. He's choosing a side and can't say why. Beat: a defector's trembling first step.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide, the Narrow Way
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Tide four: she threads the Kestrel through a channel that shouldn't hold her draft, guided by her mother's annotations, and moors inside the lagoon behind the reef. Rell's demolition crew arrives to find her already in the fortress only she can enter. Beat: the invisible woman made unignorable.

chapters.title: Siege at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel/Toma. Rell offers Toma the boat and a pardon to walk away; Toma instead cuts the Kestrel's mooring lines loose to let her drift as cover while Ansel dives on the fifth tide. Beat: loyalty chosen in the open, at real cost.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide, the Meridian
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Inside the flooded cave, she reaches the wreck and finds her father's logbook in the captain's cabin — the last entry names her mother as the saboteur who scuttled the Meridian to hide the salvage fraud Rell and her father ran together. Everyone she inherited was guilty. Beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The storm hits with the sixth tide still hours away. Rell, refusing to quit, attempts the cave entrance and loses a barge; Ansel, holding the logbook, must decide whether to let him drown or fire a line to his crew. She fires the line. Beat: mercy as the harder choice.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide, the Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the sixth tide she surfaces with the logbook and gives it to Rell and the fleet's own surveyor — surrendering all salvage rights, keeping nothing but the truth. Rell, broken by the record of his own fraud, lets the Kestrel go. Beat: victory by relinquishing.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. The storm passes. Toma repairs the Kestrel and watches Ansel burn her forged papers on the stove, keeping only the logbook and her father's chart. Vey departs with the fleet; the lockkeeper's debt is repaid. Beat: the crew exhales, changed.

chapters.title: Moored
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel moors the Kestrel at Greyhaven, registers under her true name, and takes the pilot commission she once fled. She visits her mother's grave and leaves the chart's second-hand pages there. The river still calls — but now, staying is a choice, not a defeat. Beat: inheritance reclaimed, identity whole.
